- Cross-Functional Feedback: Act as a trusted technical voice, listening carefully to customers to provide structured market feedback to the Product team to prioritise functionality and drive sales opportunities.

- Support customers throughout their trial process with Vanta.

title: Clinical Project Manager
description:
Beaufort seeks a skilled Clinical Project Manager (CPM) to work alongside a top-notch team of clinical researchers. We participate in an exciting and growing industry and that growth fuels the need to continue to build our team and support our mission.

This is a unique opportunity to join a growing CRO where your leadership will directly impact trial success and client satisfaction.

Position Summary

The Clinical Project Manager (CPM) leads the end-to-end delivery of clinical trials across diverse therapeutic areas, ensuring strategic alignment, operational excellence, and regulatory compliance. This role serves as a cross-functional leader and primary liaison between sponsors, vendors, and internal teams to drive successful trial outcomes.

Key Responsibilities

Clinical Trial Oversight & Leadership

• Provide strategic and operational oversight for assigned clinical studies from start-up through close-out.

• Lead the cross-functional project team (e.g., clinical operations, data management, statistics, safety, and medical writing) to meet or exceed project goals.

• Act as primary contact for Sponsors and serve as a Subject Matter Expert (SME) for designated clinical programs.

• Ensure compliance with ICH-GCP, SOPs, protocols, and regulatory requirements.

Project Management

• Create, manage, and maintain detailed project plans including timelines, deliverables, KPIs, and milestones.

• Track project performance using appropriate systems, tools, and techniques (e.g., project dashboards, risk logs, scope change trackers).

• Identify project risks and develop proactive mitigation strategies in collaboration with sponsors and internal stakeholders.

• Implement structured change control processes to manage protocol amendments or scope changes.

• Lead regular internal and sponsor-facing status meetings, ensuring clear communication of project progress, challenges, and action items.

Project Financial Management

• Monitor and reconcile project budgets.

• Collaborate with finance teams to provide accurate forecasts and manage scope creep.

• Support financial performance analysis.

Site and Vendor Management

• Oversee site selection activities and review feasibility data to make final recommendations.

• Provide oversight and guidance to CRAs regarding monitoring activities, site management, and issue resolution.

• Participate in or lead site qualification visits, initiation visits, interim monitoring visits, and close-out visits as needed.

• Manage vendor performance and coordinate outsourced service providers to ensure quality and timelines.

Documentation and Reporting

• Review and/or contribute to key study documents such as protocols, CRFs, monitoring plans, site manuals, and data management plans.

• Ensure timely development and delivery of study reports, metrics, and sponsor communications.

• Support regulatory submissions and audit readiness activities.

Team Support and Organizational Collaboration

• Mentor junior team members, support team knowledge sharing and contribute to performance feedback.

• Assist with onboarding, and training of new clinical operations staff.

• Provide support for business development activities, participate in bid defenses and potential client meetings as needed.

Qualifications

Education & Certifications

• Bachelor’s degree in biological sciences, pharmacy, nursing, or a related health discipline required; advanced degree preferred.

• Certification(s) such as PMP, CCRP, CCRA, or equivalent highly preferred.

Experience

• Minimum of 5 years’ experience in clinical research with at least 3 years in a project management role.

• Proven history of leading complex global or domestic clinical trials within a CRO or sponsor environment.

• Experience managing clinical studies in in vitro diagnostics (IVD) and Medical Device

• Applied deep knowledge of ICH-GCP and global regulatory requirements to ensure compliance across all phases of clinical trial execution.

DEINE ROLLE

- Du verantwortest das Wachstum in deiner Region und bist die zentrale Ansprechperson vor Ort

- Vor Ort ermittelst du den Bedarf des Salons mithilfe von Fragen und zeigst anhand von Produktdemos, wie Salonkee den Alltag vereinfachen kann.

- Du verantwortest deinen eigenen Funnel vom Erstkontakt bis zum Abschluss.

- Deine Woche planst du eigenverantwortlich, mit klaren Zielen und einer Führungskraft, die dich unterstützt und weiterentwickelt.

- Nachweisbare erste Erfahrung im Vertrieb, idealerweise mit Outbound-Anteil (Kaltakquise, Walk-ins, eigene Terminierung).

- Du bist in der Lage, Menschen zu begeistern und Interessen zu wecken.

- Du kannst mit Ablehnung umgehen und richtest den Blick nach vorn.

- Du bist lernbereit, setzt Feedback um und willst dich weiterentwickeln.

- Du bist strukturiert, organisiert und sicher im Umgang mit digitalen Tools.

- Verhandlungssicheres bis muttersprachliches Deutsch sowie gute Englischkenntnisse.

- Führerschein der Klasse B und Freude daran, in deiner Region unterwegs zu sein.

DAS ERWARTET DICH BEI UNS

- Ein Team vor Ort: Team Lead und Kolleg:innen in deiner Region - du startest nicht allein.

- Strukturierte Einarbeitung und praxisnahe Begleitung über die ersten Monate hinweg (Ramp-Up Programm).

- Ein klarer Entwicklungspfad: Von Junior über Senior bis hin zu Führungsrollen.

- Klare KPIs & Performance-Transparenz, damit du jederzeit weißt, wo du stehst.

- Eigenverantwortliche Wochenplanung und Vertrauensarbeitszeit.

- Firmenwagen inkl. Tankkarte sowie MacBook und iPhone.

- 50 € steuerfreies Guthaben pro Monat über Probonio.

- Fixgehalt und ungedeckelte Provision.

- Teamevents, die ihren Namen verdienen: Sommerfest, Winterfeier und regelmäßige Teamformate.

WIE GEHT ES WEITER?

1. Bewerbung & Sichtung - wir melden uns so schnell wie möglich bei dir.

2. Erstgespräch mit unserem Recruiting-Team (ca. 30-45 Minuten).

3. Video-Call mit deiner künftigen Führungskraft.

4. Field Day - zwei Stunden bei uns im Office. Du siehst, wie wir arbeiten, wir sehen dich in Aktion.

5. Abschlussgespräch mit unserer Head of Sales.

Salonkee steht für Chancengleichheit und Vielfalt. Wir freuen uns über Bewerbungen von Menschen mit unterschiedlichen Hintergründen, Perspektiven und Fähigkeiten - unabhängig von Geschlecht, Herkunft, Alter, Behinderung, Religion oder Identität.

title: Strike Engineer
description:
Thanks for your interest in Oklo! We are searching for a Strike Engineer to join our engineering team.

Position Description

The Strike Engineer is a senior, highly adaptable engineer who reports to the Engineering Strike Team Lead and takes ownership of Oklo's highest-priority, most ambiguous technical problems. This person moves between programs, builds context quickly, reduces problems to first principles, and stays accountable through verified resolution. Depending on the need, the Strike Engineer may serve as a hands-on individual contributor, technical lead, or interim manager. They establish a durable path, help staff the work, transfer ownership to the right long-term team, and then take on the next priority.

Specific responsibilities may include:

• Embed in high-priority engineering programs and rapidly develop a working understanding of the system, constraints, stakeholders, and current failure modes.

• Define problems from first principles by separating facts from assumptions, identifying the governing physics and interfaces, and reducing uncertainty to testable questions.

• Work hands-on across design, analysis, prototyping, testing, manufacturing, software and data, systems integration, and field execution as the problem requires.

• Establish a practical execution plan with owners, decision points, schedule, risks, and objective completion criteria, then drive the work through verified closure.

• Diagnose technical and operational failures using data, experiments, direct observation, and disciplined root-cause analysis.

• Make sound engineering tradeoffs under uncertainty while accounting for safety, regulatory requirements, quality, cost, schedule, operability, and manufacturability.

• Temporarily lead a project or team when needed by clarifying priorities, coordinating cross-functional work, removing blockers, and communicating decisions and risks.

• Help recruit and onboard permanent owners, then transfer stable scope with clear documentation, open risks, decisions, and next steps.

• Create reusable tools, processes, design standards, or technical documentation when they will prevent recurring problems or accelerate future work.

Minimum Qualifications:

• Bachelor's degree in engineering, physics, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.

• 2 or more years of experience solving complex engineering problems from definition through design, execution, validation, and handoff.

• Technical breadth across multiple engineering domains and deep expertise in at least one area such as mechanical, electrical, controls, software, systems, manufacturing, test, thermal-fluid, structural, or nuclear engineering.

• Demonstrated ability to reason from first principles, challenge unsupported assumptions, and validate conclusions with analysis, tests, or operating data.

• Hands-on ability to use the tools needed to move work forward, which may include modeling, CAD, calculations, test equipment, scripting, data analysis, or prototyping.

• Experience leading cross-functional technical work without relying on formal authority, including stepping into temporary management responsibilities when needed.

• Strong written and verbal communication, including concise decision records, technical plans, risk summaries, and executive-level updates.

Bonus Qualifications:

• Experience in the nuclear industry, advanced reactor development, commercial power generation, national laboratories, or another safety-critical energy environment.

• Experience delivering hardware or integrated systems in a regulated, high-consequence, or quality-controlled environment.

• Experience starting a new program, recovering a stalled project, or resolving a persistent technical or operational problem.

• Experience with hardware-software integration, automation, controls, data systems, or test infrastructure.

• Experience hiring, developing, or onboarding engineers and transferring work to a durable long-term owner.

title: Founding Legal Counsel
description:
Hi 👋 I'm Ellis, COO at Pinpoint .

We're a high growth HR tech company building software that helps in house recruitment teams attract, hire, and onboard the right talent. Today we have a strong foundation in place: a mature product, rapid growth, strong product market fit, and happy customers. We've built strong operational foundations, but we've never had a dedicated lawyer. Legal work has been landing on the ops team, and the volume is climbing fast: contract volume is up sharply, and the product is moving into even more regulated territory. We need someone to own the legal end to end so our deals keep moving and our customers stay confident. That's where you come in.

The fine print (but way more exciting):

• This is a remote role based in the UK with occasional in-person team meetups.

• You'll be our first dedicated legal hire, so you're building the function and inheriting the old contracts and processes at the same time.

• You'll be the sole member of the legal team and will own both the judgment and the tactical. work: marking up contracts, chasing signatures, building templates, and staying on top of compliance.

• There's no one to delegate to, and there's no escalation for the day-to-day slog.

• The volume is heavy, and the pace is fast. This role suits someone who likes to build and who's hands-on; it's not a quiet compliance desk.

• Our values actually matter here. We hire people who reflect them in how they work, collaborate, and make decisions.

About the Role:

Sales legal (35%)

• Own commercial contracting end to end: our MSA, DPA, and customer red lines. You're who the Account Executives bring a marked up agreement to, and you're who closes it out

• Turn around a high volume of reviews at pace. Contract volume is spiking, driven by growth and by the rise in AI usage, and we need someone commercial and pragmatic to own it

• Set and publish a legal SLA for sales, so turnaround is a promise, not a guess

• Own our risk tolerance and playbook: liability caps, indemnities, termination. Know where we flex, where we hold, and when to escalate

• Run legal intake: triage what needs you, what sales can self serve, and what genuinely needs external counsel

• Build the playbooks, fallback positions, and templates that let AEs answer the easy questions without you

Product legal (20%)

• Partner with Product and Engineering as we build in a regulated space: background screening, right to work, DBS and credit checks, and AI-assisted hiring features

• Own regulatory compliance as the landscape shifts: UK and EU GDPR, FCRA, the EU AI Act, and a growing patchwork of US state law

Partnerships, NDAs, and supplier terms (15%)

• Draft and negotiate partnership, reseller, and referral agreements, including integration and marketplace partners

• Own NDAs, supplier and vendor terms, and the contract lifecycle from template to signature to renewal

• Negotiate with suppliers and integration partners so those terms stay robust and commercial

Data protection, governance, and audit readiness (30%)

• Own data protection across the business: our DPA, sub processor management, DPIAs, DSARs, records of processing, and international transfers

• Keep us on the right side of UK and EU GDPR, US state privacy law, and the local regimes that surface in deals (Quebec Law 25 and China's PIPL are recent examples)

• Make audit readiness a habit, not a scramble, with policies that reflect what we actually do

• Lead due diligence readiness: corporate housekeeping, share and option documentation, and cleaning up historic contractual exposure before someone else finds it

About You:

• A qualified lawyer (England and Wales, or an equivalent common law jurisdiction) with real commercial contracting experience, including in-house time at a SaaS business

• Experience as in-house counsel in a scaling startup (50-250 people) where you've built legal infrastructure from limited resources and moved at fast pace

title: International Growth Marketing Manager
locationText: France, Germany, Italy, Spain, United Kingdom
description:
iFIT ’s vision is to create the world's most holistic health and fitness platform, integrating all elements of health - physical fitness, mental health, nutrition and active recovery - into a seamless interactive experience. We develop proprietary software that learns and adjusts to the habits of each person as it delivers immersive content that guides them on their own individual fitness journey.

We run marketing across five European markets - the UK, France, Germany, Spain, and Italy - spanning the full channel mix: paid social, paid search, affiliate, influencer, retail media, and OTT/programmatic/linear TV, plus organic/AEO presence in every market. Today, the Sr Director of Global Paid Media personally owns strategy for Europe on top of running the US business. That doesn't scale across five markets with different competitive dynamics, maturity, and channel mix - the right move is a dedicated strategic owner for Europe, not a copy-pasted US playbook stretched across five countries.
We're hiring that owner. You won't run campaigns - the discipline specialists on the paid media team (affiliate, influencer, paid social, paid search, retail media, OTT) already execute at a high level across every market, and they keep doing that. What's missing is the person who decides, market by market, what those specialists should be doing and why: the channel mix for Spain versus Germany, where the next incremental dollar goes between countries, which markets are under-invested versus just under-measured, and how to tell the difference.
This is primarily a strategist-and-manager role - the discipline specialists are the default owners of execution, and you don't need to be the best person in the building at building the campaign itself. But it's a player-coach role, not a pure strategy seat: specialist attention is a shared, limited resource, and some work (a market that needs attention faster than the queue can give it, a test only one market needs, a gap no one else is positioned to close) will land on you to execute directly rather than wait on. You need broad, credible working knowledge of every channel we use - enough to direct a specialist, catch a bad plan, reallocate budget across channels and countries with judgment, and pick up the tool yourself when a market needs it faster than a handoff allows.
What you'll do
Strategy & budget ownership (~40%)

• Own the European marketing budget end to end: allocation across channels and markets, reforecasting, and the quarterly story to leadership on where spend is going and why.

• Build a real market-by-market strategy - channel mix, funnel priorities, and growth plan sized to each market's maturity, competitive set, and retail/DTC mix. Five countries, not one template stretched across all of them.

• Make the channel trade-off calls with judgment: when a market's paid search is saturating, when affiliate commission structures need to flex by country, when OTT earns a slot in a market's mix and when it doesn't.

Directing execution (~30%)

• Turn strategy into clear briefs and priorities for the discipline specialists who execute European work - you own the “what and why,” they own the “how.”

• Run the operating cadence: regular reviews per market, catch underperformance early, and reprioritize specialist time across markets when one country needs more attention than another.

• Keep paid and organic coherent per market - partner with SEO/AEO and, where they exist, in-market teams or agencies.

Performance & measurement (~20%)

• Own the European performance narrative - ROAS, CAC, revenue, share of spend by market and channel - held to the same rigor as the US business.

• Partner with marketing science/analytics to get a real read on European channel performance instead of platform-reported numbers; several markets don't have mature measurement yet, and closing that gap is part of the job.

It includes a medication and medical history review, a physical evaluation, and, if ordered by the person’s health plan, additional diagnostic tests (i.e., diabetic eye exams, spirometry, etc.). • Conduct virtual visits as needed

• Provide all Signify Health services as indicated including Diagnostic & Preventive Services products (i.e., spirometry, DEE, bone density screening, etc.)

A Note on Our Work Environment:
As an in-home clinician, your primary workplace is the private residence of health plan members. We are dedicated to meeting health plan members where they are, wherever they call home. These environments are diverse and may present a variety of conditions. Candidates must be able to comfortably and safely perform their duties in homes that may contain household pets, secondhand smoke and other potential airborne allergens or irritants.
Why Clinicians Enjoy Working with Signify Health
“Many of the people I see are shocked that a physician is coming to their home to visit with them one-on-one. When you sit down and have an unhurried conversation about their health, they are impressed, happy, and understand that their health plan and care team cares about them.” - M.L., MD
“The primary care physician gets a snapshot of a person in an office setting, but with Signify Health, we see things like the number of steps to enter their home, the state of disrepair those steps may be in, and the person’s ability to function comfortably and with ease in their own home. We can make referrals to the individual’s health plan, encourage the participation of their loved ones, and ensure their PCPs are aware of their health and overall quality of life.” - C.H., MD

About JumpCloud®
JumpCloud® is the AI-powered unified IT management platform designed to secure the modern workforce. By consolidating identity, device, and access management, JumpCloud provides intelligent, secure IT that scales from human users to autonomous AI agents. We help organizations around the globe eliminate complexity and turn AI risk into an optimized advantage, ensuring the right people and agents have secure access to the right resources at all times.
 
JumpCloud is Intelligent, Secure IT.

The role
Every organization now runs on identities, devices and, increasingly, AI agents. Someone has to decide who and what gets access to what, and keep it secure. At JumpCloud, that is often a small IT team responsible for an entire workforce across Mac, Windows, Linux and mobile, using one platform in place of several. For them, the experience is the product. When it is clear, a lean team runs what once took a stack of tools and a much larger staff. When it is not, people get locked out and risks go unseen.
That experience will change more in the next two years than in the last ten. Admins will ask an assistant instead of opening a console. AI agents will need identities, permissions and oversight of their own. Some of our most important experiences will have no screen at all.
We are looking for the design leader who will define what comes next. You will set the experience vision for the platform, decide where design invests across the interface, AI and headless experiences, and build a team known for its craft and its judgment. title: Senior Director of Curriculum
description:
CodePath is the largest educator of college computer science students in the country. We've trained over 40,000 students from 1,000+ universities, and our partners include Amazon, Google, and other leading technology companies. We've spent nearly a decade training the next generation of technical talent, and we just launched a $150M initiative with Anthropic, building one of the most ambitious AI workforce programs in the world.

We're now expanding into new markets and scaling our team so we can move at the speed AI is transforming the workforce. People joining CodePath now will have the opportunity to help architect the next frontier of our work.

We believe technical skill is the fastest way to turn raw talent into real opportunity. We train the engineers the AI era runs on, building toward millions of learners, hundreds of millions in revenue, and billions in economic impact. If you want to own something and be part of a 0-to-1 journey at an organization moving at the speed of AI, this is the place to build it.

About the Role
Location: Remote, United States
Role Type: Full-Time
Reporting to: Chief Product Officer
Total Compensation: $165,000 to $239,000 per year

• Base salary: $165,000 to $200,000

• Total compensation includes the base salary plus a guaranteed supplement

The Senior Director of Curriculum is a senior leadership role responsible for the vision, strategy, and execution of CodePath ’s entire curriculum portfolio. You will set long-term curriculum direction while directly shaping high-impact courses, particularly in AI-native software engineering, technical interview preparation, cybersecurity, and web development.
You will partner closely with Learning (Programs & Student Experience), Engineering, Platform, Revenue, and Employer Partnerships to ensure CodePath courses remain rigorous, engaging, and aligned to rapidly evolving industry needs. You will own the systems, processes, roadmap and initially manage a small, high-impact team and own hiring as the function scales that allow CodePath to move faster without compromising quality.
Check out our Course Catalog and our 2024 Annual Report to learn more!
Software engineering is changing faster than traditional academic programs can adapt. Generative AI is reshaping how engineers design, build, debug, and ship software-and employers increasingly expect new graduates to be AI-native from day one.
As Director of Curriculum, you will define how CodePath bridges the gap between academic computer science programs and industry expectations. You will lead the transition to a more modular, flexible curriculum architecture that enables rapid iteration, targeted updates, and new delivery models across:

• Undergraduate, for-credit university partnerships

• Undergraduate, Direct-to-student programs

• Employer-focused upskilling and reskilling offerings

Our programs, run both online and in-person, begin with inspiration and build toward technical excellence and practical mastery, supported by learning pathways and strong student support systems. Our curriculum is grounded in proven learning principles - proper leveling, balanced pacing, spaced repetition, blended synchronous and asynchronous learning, peer collaboration, and project-based work.
You will define how we prepare students to become AI-native software engineers and steward our course portfolio to support CodePath ’s growth from 20,000 to 100,000 students per year.
Key Responsibilities
Curriculum Strategy & Portfolio Ownership

• Lead CodePath ’s long-term curriculum strategy and transition to a modular, flexible architecture that supports AI- native skills, rapid iteration, and multiple delivery models

• Own the curriculum product roadmap, maintaining 12-month visibility into new courses, major revisions, and portfolio investments

• Maintain and evolve a comprehensive course catalog across Web Development, Mobile Development, Cybersecurity, Technical Interview Prep, Foundational CS, and AI-native offering

Description

• Performs appeal and retrospective reviews demonstrating ability to define and determine precedence of pertinent issues in application of policies and procedures to clinical information and or application to benefit or policy provisions.

description:
Company Overview:
Our client is a small, founder-led consumer brand based in Austin, TX, that makes a regulated nicotine product (tobacco-free pouches) and sells it direct-to-consumer in the UK. Because Meta, Google, and TikTok all prohibit nicotine advertising, there is no ad budget this company can spend to buy growth - every channel that's left (search, owned email and SMS, subscription retention, referral, retail and trade, athlete and podcast partnerships, field sampling) has to be built and wired together by hand. That constraint is the whole shape of this job.
Your Role:
This role exists because the easy version of growth marketing isn't available here - someone has to build the campaign machinery, not just brief it. You'll spend real time each week directing Claude Code to connect APIs, enrich lists, and automate recurring work, and the rest of your time running campaigns alongside the people actually knocking on doors: sales, field, and partnerships. You report directly to the two founders, at manager level, fully hands-on, with no reports of your own (headcount comes later, if at all). Success looks like a trade and partnership outbound engine that runs itself, a field team that's armed and getting better each cycle, owned channels (search, lifecycle, retention, referral) doing the growth work that paid acquisition can't, and numbers everyone can actually trust.
A note on the category: this is a regulated product, and the rules aren't style guidance - they're hard constraints on the job itself. No health, cessation, or performance claims anywhere, ever. Age and territory gating (18+, UK only) stays intact, full stop. No paid social or paid search for the product, no workarounds. Nothing overstated in writing. If that reads as a limitation on the work rather than the actual shape of it, this isn't the right seat.
You'll:

• Build and run the trade and partnership outbound engine - define the segment, pull and enrich the list, verify and score contacts, write and track the sequence, and know when not to use a sequencer (some outreach has to go out by hand)

• Arm the field team (sampling, shop visits, trade shows) with target lists, routes, one-pagers, and post-visit follow-up sequences, then work alongside them so the next version is better

• Own the channels that are actually open here: search and content, lifecycle email and SMS, subscription retention (win-back, dunning recovery, pause-instead-of-cancel), and referral programs, including the reconciliation behind them

• Produce creative in-house with AI tools against the brand's existing visual system - knowing when to generate, when to composite a real product shot instead, and when to send a piece to a human

• Automate anything manual and recurring - enrichment scripts, list hygiene, report pulls, campaign QA, content pipelines - instead of adding it to someone's checklist

• Own first-party measurement (order and subscription data, cohort retention, referral attribution, search visibility), since no ad platform is feeding this business conversion data, and flag a bad number before anyone else finds it

You Bring:

• Real, hands-on experience directing Claude Code (or an equivalent coding agent) on live work - connected to an API or MCP server, shipping something still in use today. This is the one non-negotiable requirement on this list, and it's tested directly in the interview process; nearly everything else here is trainable

title: Trust Communications
description:
TL;DR

Millions of people build on Lovable, from software that runs new businesses to the tools that power existing ones. At the center of it all is trust. That’s why we’re looking for an exceptional storyteller to spearhead Lovable’s trust, safety, and security communications efforts.

WHY LOVABLE

For decades, the ability to build software belonged to a tiny fraction of the population: the people with the credentials, the technical training, the access. Everyone else had to wait, or pay, or give up. Lovable is the counterargument: We exist for the people with ideas who were locked out of software creation until now.

Over 70 million projects have been built on the platform. Hundreds of thousands of people pay for it. The product handles real infrastructure, not only prototypes: authentication, databases, payments, and deployment. People run real businesses on Lovable, which means the stakes are real too.

The comms challenge: when anyone can build, the platform has to be safe for everyone who does, and they need to know it. That takes someone who can tell the story of how we think about topics like safety, security, and reliability before anyone asks, and who can be honest, precise, and fast when the questions come up anyway.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

Build and own Lovable’s trust narrative. You’ll own Lovable’s trust narrative in earned, new, and owned media, proactively telling the story of how we think about security, privacy, and safety. You’ll shape the stories that highlight our commitments and ensure we show up in the conversations where trust in AI platforms is being decided right now.

Be the comms partner to our security and trust leadership. You’ll develop and own the spokesperson platforms for our CISO and other senior leaders who speak on our trust efforts, identifying and preparing them for on-stage and media opportunities. You’ll help them become recognized voices on topics of trust in AI software creation.

Own incident communications, end to end. When something doesn’t go as planned, you’re the incident comms lead who ensures clear and swift communications for every audience that needs to hear from us, including media, customers, and employees. You’ll build and run the playbook that lets us move faster each time.

Build relationships with relevant media and creators. You’ll know the voices who matter most in telling our trust story, and you’ll make sure those relationships exist before we need them.

WHO YOU ARE

You’ve done trust, safety, or security communications. You have proven comms experience across a variety of trust-related topics, from AI safety to security. You’ve worked on or alongside security, privacy, or trust and safety teams.

You have real incident experience. You’ve been the incident comms lead more than once, and you’ve probably written a playbook along the way. You bring the attention to detail, precision, speed, and judgment an incident requires.

You have strong media relationships in the tech and AI ecosystem. Security and trust reporters, analysts, policy-adjacent media, perhaps even researchers. You know who they are, what they care about, and how to earn their attention honestly.

We’re looking for a sharp, driven, problem-solving Senior Software Engineer (Ruby on Rails) to join our engineering team.

While your primary focus will be backend development, we value engineers who are T-shaped, bringing deep expertise in one area while being comfortable contributing in others. Whether that means diving into frontend code, supporting mobile efforts, or lending an extra set of eyes in discovery, you’ll collaborate with your teammates to move work forward.

Most importantly, you’ll actively contribute to the evolution of the culture and processes of a growing engineering team, especially our backend engineering discipline. We want senior devs with experience effectively scaling codebases and iterating on processes as part of a growing team and with interest in mentoring to help our devs grow, too.

title: Research Intern
description:
ABOUT US

Sierra is the leading platform for customer-facing AI agents, working with many of the world's biggest brands - including The GAP, Rocket Mortgage, SoFi, Sutter Health, and SoftBank - to transform how they serve customers and grow their businesses. We are primarily an in-person company based in San Francisco, with growing offices across North America, Europe, and Asia.

We are guided by a set of values that are at the core of our actions and define our culture: Trust, Customer Obsession, Craftsmanship, Intensity, and a commitment to balancing Family along the way. These values are the foundation of our work, and we are committed to upholding them in everything we do.

Our co-founders are Bret Taylor https://www.linkedin.com/in/brettaylor/ and Clay Bavor https://www.linkedin.com/in/claybavor/. Bret currently serves as Board Chair of OpenAI. Previously, he was co-CEO of Salesforce (which had acquired the company he founded, Quip) and CTO of Facebook. Bret was also one of Google's earliest product managers and co-creator of Google Maps. Before founding Sierra, Clay spent 18 years at Google, where he most recently led Google Labs. Earlier, he started and led Google’s AR/VR effort, Project Starline, and Google Lens. Before that, Clay led the product and design teams for Google Workspace.

Sierra’s Applied Research team works to make the models behind our agents better, faster, and cheaper across many kinds of tasks. Our work covers post-training open-weight models for specialized capabilities, new approaches to voice AI, and the benchmarks the field uses to measure agents, including τ-bench.

As an Applied Research Intern, you’ll join the team for a research project, working with a mentor, you’ll pick a problem that matters to how AI agents perform in the real world, run rigorous experiments, and potentially write up what you find for a top venue. If you want your research to reach both the research community and production agents used by millions of people, come do it at Sierra.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

- Own a research project from start to finish, from framing the question and running experiments to writing and submitting a paper.

- Push agent evaluation forward, for example by extending τ-bench to new domains, modalities, or long-horizon tasks, or by building new ways to measure reliability and consistency.

- Study how agents reason, use tools, and follow policies over multi-turn conversations, and find out where and why they fail.

- Explore post-training methods such as supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning to improve agent behavior, and measure the gains rigorously.

- Work with large-scale, proprietary datasets of text and audio interactions to find research questions grounded in real customer problems.

- Work with researchers and engineers across Sierra, and where it makes sense, turn your findings into improvements in production.

WHAT YOU’LL BRING

- Currently pursuing a PhD in computer science, machine learning, or a related field.

- A research track record, such as first-author publications or submissions at venues like NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, ACL, EMNLP, Interspeech or ICASSP.

- Strong experimental skills: you design clean experiments, build careful baselines, and are honest about what the results do and do not show.

- Fluency in Python and modern ML tooling (for example, PyTorch, and LLM inference and training stacks).

- High agency and a builder’s mindset. You’ll work across the stack to get an experiment running.

- Clear, direct communication, both in writing and when presenting research.

EVEN BETTER

- Research experience with LLM agents, tool use, or multi-turn dialogue.

- Experience designing benchmarks or evaluations, especially ones tied to real-world outcomes.

- Experience with supervised fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, or long-horizon optimization.

- Experience with speech, voice, or multimodal models.

- Open-source contributions to ML research code or benchmarks.
